Vayera 1: Avraham, three days after his bris, runs to welcome three guests and serves them a meal. One of them promises that Sarah will have a son by next year, and Sarah laughs.
Vayera 2: Sarah denies that she laughed. Hashem tells Avraham He is about to judge Sedom, and Avraham pleads for the city: for fifty righteous people, then fewer, down to ten.
Vayera 3: The two angels reach Sedom and Lot takes them in. The townspeople surround the house, the angels strike them blind, and at dawn they lead Lot and his family out. Lot asks to flee to a small town nearby.
Vayera 4: Sedom is destroyed and Lot's wife becomes a pillar of salt; Lot's daughters give birth to Moav and Amon. Avimelech takes Sarah and is warned in a dream to return her. Sarah gives birth to Yitzchak, and Avraham gives him a bris at eight days.
Vayera 5: Sarah rejoices in her son. At the feast for Yitzchak's weaning, Sarah tells Avraham to send away Hagar and Yishmael; Hashem agrees, and in the desert an angel shows Hagar a well.
Vayera 6: Avimelech asks Avraham for a treaty. They settle a dispute over a well with seven sheep and swear at Be'er Sheva, where Avraham plants an eshel and calls in the Name of Hashem.
Vayera 7: The Akeidah: Hashem tells Avraham to bring Yitzchak as an offering. An angel stops him at the last moment, a ram is offered instead, and Hashem blesses Avraham. News comes of Nachor's family, Rivka among them.
Chayei Sara 1: Sarah passes away at 127. Avraham asks the people of Ches for a burial place, and buys the Cave of Machpelah from Efron for four hundred silver shekels.
Chayei Sara 2: Avraham buries Sarah in the Cave of Machpelah. Then, old and blessed in everything, he makes his servant swear to find a wife for Yitzchak from his own family, not from Canaan.
Chayei Sara 3: The servant reaches the well in Aram Naharayim and asks Hashem for a sign: the girl who offers water to him and to his camels. Rivka does just that, and he bows in thanks.
Chayei Sara 4: Rivka's brother Lavan welcomes the servant. Before eating he tells the whole story, and Lavan and Besuel answer: this is from Hashem; take Rivka.
Chayei Sara 5: Rivka agrees to go, and her family blesses her. Toward evening Yitzchak goes out to pray in the field and sees the camels coming; he marries Rivka and is comforted after his mother.
Chayei Sara 6: Avraham marries Keturah and has more sons, sends them away with gifts and leaves everything to Yitzchak. He passes away at 175, and Yitzchak and Yishmael bury him in the Cave of Machpelah.
Chayei Sara 7: Yishmael's twelve sons, leaders of their tribes, and his death at 137.
Toldot 1: Yitzchak prays for children and Rivka has twins who struggle inside her; Hashem tells her two nations will come from them. Eisav, tired from the field, sells his birthright to Yaakov for lentil stew. In a famine, Hashem tells Yitzchak not to go down to Egypt.
Toldot 2: In Gerar, Yitzchak says Rivka is his sister. Avimelech sees the truth and warns his people not to touch them. Yitzchak plants and reaps a hundredfold.
Toldot 3: Yitzchak grows very rich; the jealous Philistines stop up Avraham's wells and send him away. He reopens his father's wells and digs new ones: two bring quarrels, and the third he names Rechovos.
Toldot 4: In Be'er Sheva Hashem appears to Yitzchak and promises to bless him, and he builds an altar. Avimelech comes with his general to ask for a treaty.
Toldot 5: They make the treaty, and Yitzchak's servants find water at Shiva. Eisav marries Hittite women. Old and blind, Yitzchak asks Eisav for a meal before blessing him; Rivka dresses Yaakov in Eisav's clothes, and Yitzchak blesses him.
Toldot 6: The blessing of dew and plenty. Eisav comes back and cries out, and Yitzchak blesses him too. Eisav plans to kill Yaakov, so Rivka sends him to Lavan, and Yitzchak blesses Yaakov again with the blessing of Avraham.
Toldot 7: Yaakov sets out for Padan Aram. Eisav sees that the daughters of Canaan displease his father, and marries a daughter of Yishmael.
Vayetzei 1: Yaakov leaves Be'er Sheva for Charan. He sleeps at "the place" and dreams of a ladder with angels; Hashem promises him the land, children and protection. He wakes, calls it Beis El, and vows a tenth.
Vayetzei 2: At a well near Charan, Yaakov rolls the stone off for Rachel, waters her sheep and weeps. Lavan welcomes him, and after a month asks what wage he wants. Leah and Rachel are described.
Vayetzei 3: Yaakov works seven years for Rachel, and Lavan gives him Leah. He marries Rachel a week later and works seven more years. Leah has Reuven, Shimon, Levi and Yehudah; through Bilhah and Zilpah come Dan, Naftali, Gad and Asher.
Vayetzei 4: Reuven's dudaim. Leah has Yissachar, Zevulun and Dinah. Hashem remembers Rachel and she has Yosef. Yaakov asks to go home, and Lavan says Hashem blessed him because of Yaakov.
Vayetzei 5: The wage agreement: the speckled and spotted flocks are Yaakov's, and his peeled rods make them grow. Lavan's sons resent it, Hashem tells Yaakov to return, and Rachel and Leah agree to go.
Vayetzei 6: Yaakov leaves secretly and Rachel takes Lavan's idols. Lavan chases him, but Hashem warns him in a dream. Lavan searches and finds nothing, and Yaakov answers him: twenty years of faithful work.
Vayetzei 7: Yaakov and Lavan make a covenant over a pile of stones, Gal-Ed. Lavan kisses his grandchildren and goes home, and angels meet Yaakov at Machanayim.
Vayishlach 1: Yaakov sends messengers to Eisav, who is coming with four hundred men. Afraid, Yaakov splits his camp in two and prays: "I am too small for all Your kindness."
Vayishlach 2: Yaakov sends Eisav a gift of animals, herd after herd. At night he crosses the Yabok, and a man wrestles with him until dawn, hurts his thigh, and names him Yisrael.
Vayishlach 3: Yaakov names the place Peniel, which is why we don't eat the gid hanasheh. He sees Eisav coming, bows seven times, and Eisav runs to him and hugs him, and they cry.
Vayishlach 4: The family bows to Eisav, and Yaakov presses him to take the gift. Eisav goes back to Se'ir; Yaakov builds shelters at Sukkos, then comes safely to Shechem, buys a field and builds an altar.
Vayishlach 5: Shechem takes Dinah. Her brothers demand that the city be circumcised, then Shimon and Levi kill its men, and Yaakov rebukes them. At Beis El Hashem blesses Yaakov and confirms the name Yisrael.
Vayishlach 6: Rachel dies giving birth to Binyamin and is buried on the way to Efras. Yaakov's twelve sons are listed. Yitzchak dies at 180, and Eisav and Yaakov bury him. Eisav's family and chiefs.
Vayishlach 7: The families of Se'ir the Chori, the kings who ruled in Edom before Israel had a king, and the chiefs of Eisav.
